regional_calque_anchors.etymology: Already established primary calque (*szék* = throne/chair $\rightarrow$ *Stuhl*; *fehér* = white $\rightarrow$ *weiß*; *vár* = castle $\rightarrow$ *Burg*).
Calque of Hungarian *Vasvár* ("Iron Castle", German *Eisenburg*) from the comital seat on the Rába.
Slavic substrate *Črnograd* ("Black Gord/Castle"), calqued root-for-root into Tarraconian.
Named after King Samuel Aba's fortress at *Abaújvár* ("Aba's New Castle").
Historical German *Zips*; pre-1059 Gord at *Čingov* on the Hornád can alternatively be calqued as *Tschingouwe*.
Pre-1059 salt-mining centre *Solotvyno* (Slavic *sol* = salt) on the Upper Tisza.
From Hungarian *békés* ("peaceful / peace-guard") or Ispán Beke; calqued as *Fridstat / Fridburch*.
Hybrid formation combining hydronym *Temes* with generic calque *-burch* (German *Temeschburg / Temeswar*).
Already established primary calque (*Cetatea Albă / Belgorod* = "White Castle on the Dniester").
Slavic *novy* ("new") + *gorod* ("city/gord"), qualified by the Volkhov river (*Wolchouwe*).
Slavic plural *soli* ("salt pans / salt mines"), later Ottoman *Tuzla*.
Slavic *mostar* ("bridge-keeper"), referring to the crossing of the Neretva.
Established alternate kingdom title calquing *Belaya Rus'* ("White Russia"), with historical resolution **Polôtzich** (Principality of Polotsk).
Pre-1256 seat *Zvenyhorod* derives from Slavic *zveneti* ("to ring/resound/chime"), calquing to *Klingeburch*.
Hydronym of the *Babruyka* ("Beaver Brook") from Slavic *bobr* ("beaver").
Pre-867 Dulebe earthwork fortress *Zimne* ("winter quarter") on the Luga River.
Slavic *pereyati slavu* ("take the glory/renown") at the Trubizh ford.
Slavic *opole* ("open fertile field/clearing amidst the deep forest").
Latin *Furnus Calcarius* ("Lime Kilns / Lime Ovens", cf. *Ofen*).
Arabic *Bahr al-Mayyit* / Hebrew *Yam Ha-Mavet* ("The Dead Sea").
Arabic *Hisn al-Akrad* ("Kurds' Fortress") $\rightarrow$ Crusader *Krak des Chevaliers*.
Hebrew *Be'er Sheva* ("Well of the Seven / Well of the Oath").
Slavic *Perekop* / Greek *Taphros* ("The Dug Trench / Isthmus Ditch").
Slavic *Němьcь* ("Germans / Saxon miners") + fortress rock *Piatra Neamț*.
Hungarian *Vaskapu* / Romanian *Porțile de Fier* ("Iron Gates of the Danube").
Already established calque of Welsh *Perfeddwlad* ("Middle Country").
Old Irish *Dubh Linn* ("Black Pool / Dark Pond").
Old Irish *Cill Dara* ("Church of the Oak Grove").
Gaelic *Inbhir Nis* ("Mouth of the River Ness").
Tibetan *mar* ("low, downward") + *yul* ("land") $\rightarrow$ "The Lowland / Lower Country" (Ladakh relative to the high Changtang plateau).
Tibetan *sPo* (the ancient kingdom of Powo / Bomê) + *yul* ("land").
